(3) MINOR issues (verbatim)

From mclass:
- "fq3_m.MU.at docstring "MConst at u = eps" is literally true only for K >= 19 (exact u-degree 18); for the production K = 6 at(eps) is the mod-u^K truncated polynomial evaluated at eps, which is NOT symplectic (at(eps, check=True) raises "not symplectic at zhat^2"). The code relies on this only through UVertex, where it is correct (truncating M^{-1} mod u^K leaves the eps^e coefficients, e < K, of every vertex tensor unchanged), but a reader could misuse at(eps) as an exact M(eps). Suggest a docstring note." Reproduction: ref6_at_check.py (K = 6 raises, K = 19 passes).
- "fq3_m.MU drops N_j with j >= K silently (`if j >= K: break`); harmless (they cannot enter mod u^K) but undocumented."
- "(4) "maximal n" is bounded by Nz = 6 only; the identity Q_a^{(i)} = Sum_j Rh^{(j)}_{a,0} C_{ji} makes R^ M_0^{-1} constant to every available order, so this check cannot fail for any Nz and is a consistency check of colour_matrix/Minv, not new information."
- "HatRowsU.min_prec is computed after truncation to K, so the production check "min_prec >= K" is equivalent to "untruncated precision >= K" — correct but reads oddly."

From graphs:
- "fq3_msum.s_to_u(ser, K): a series that is ZERO to its s-precision gets u-precision K regardless of the actual s-precision (overstated); harmless now because HatRowsU.val_ok requires every row to be non-zero with v = 0 (True in my run), but it is not asserted."
- "UVertex: Ser(R, 0, coeffs[:K]) silently claims precision K even if K > NN (only NN coefficients exist); production K=6 <= NN=21 so no effect. The degree assertion (deg <= 18) runs only when NN >= 20, so NN=19 relies on the bound unverified."
- "UVertex interpolates MVertex6(MUobj.at(e)) where .at(e) evaluates the u-TRUNCATED M (not symplectic for eps != 0,1). This is correct: the tensor is a polynomial in the M^{-1} entries, agreeing with the exact one mod eps^K, and the eps-degree of a weight-D term is <= Sum min(3k_i, K-1) <= 3D (total M-weight = D, which I checked by the dimension count Sum_v). Not a bug, but the docstring's "M = M_0 exp(eps N_1 + ...)" justification should mention that the bound survives truncation."
- "Zero placeholders in vertex_tensor use vec[0].prec (same as the genus-2 code): precision of identically-zero entries can be overstated when components have unequal precision; no effect when all rows are truncated at the same K."
- "fq3_graphs.canon brute-forces all V! permutations per degeneration: legged_graphs(3,1,5)/(1,4,4) take minutes (my compare run: 5 min total, of which the independent enumerator took < 1 s). Correctness unaffected."

Side result (mclass, tc_expansion3): "the vertex graph has polar part (1/25200) t_c^{-4} + 0 + 0 + 0 iff its u-coefficients are a_0 = 1/25200, a_1 = -1/9000, a_2 = 407/3780000, a_3 = -151/3780000 (both primes)."

- graphs: "correctness of GraphSummer6/MVertex6 numbers AT GENUS 3 by an independent reference (I only verified agreement with the genus-2 code of record, the genus-2 UVertex/MU path, and the graph/decoration combinatorics)"; "the production genus-3 values themselves."
- mclass: "The hatted count for u-DEPENDENT M (MU through rows_prime6 Ser path + UVertex): verified only algebraically ... a direct s-series evaluation with M(zhat; u) at genus 3 was not run."
- eps-degree bound: mclass "UVertex degree bound 3D <= 18: verified for the M^{-1} entries (max u-degree 18 observed), the implication for weight-D tensors is by the polynomial argument, not by a run"; graphs "the eps-degree <= 18 bound at genus 3 was argued, not measured (production NN=21 asserts it at run time)."
- Mbar_3 = 42 strata "confirmed by my enumeration only (E-distribution 1,2,5,9,12,8,5)" (graphs); not cross-checked against literature.

reports.report: Waiting on the background runs (one Python process at a time per the task constraints); the remaining checks (check2, check3) depend on that process finishing.

REFEREE REPORT — subdir mclass (fq3_m.py; genus-3 hatted-theory claims of fq3_msum.py)
Scripts (all pure Python, run as `py -I <script>`, one process at a time, each < 35 s):
C:/Users/user/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d7c1b608d03d194a/37f24460-3601-4c85-b123-5156e19eb475/scratchpad/g3referee/mclass/ref1_sp_classes.py (checks 1, 2), ref2_mu.py (check 3), ref3_symbol.py (check 4; arg 89|61), ref4_tc.py (check 5 numerics), ref5_sseries.py (check 5, direct s-series control; args "idx,idx" kmax), ref6_at_check.py (MU.at symplecticity). Primes: 2^61-1 throughout; check 4 and 5 also at 2^89-1.

(1) sp mod zhat^7 — derivation: for M = 1 + eps N(zhat) + O(eps^2), M(zhat)^T M(-zhat) = 1 + eps (N(zhat)^T + N(-zhat)) + O(eps^2), so the Lie algebra is {N : N_k^T + (-1)^k N_k = 0 for k = 1..6}, i.e. N_k symmetric for odd k (15 free entries each: k = 1, 3, 5) and antisymmetric for even k (10 each: k = 2, 4, 6), N_0 = 0; dimension 45 + 30 = 75. The group {M^T(zhat) M(-zhat) = 1} is the symplectic group of the normalised pairing (eta(e~_i, e~_j) = delta_ij, so M^*(z) = M(-z)^T), and exp maps sp into it to all orders.
CHECK sp_lie_algebra: PASS — the constraint space {N_k^T = (-1)^{k+1} N_k} over all 150 entries has F_p-nullspace dimension 75 (= NSP); exp of a random sp element (own matrix exponential) satisfies M^T(zhat) M(-zhat) = 1 mod zhat^7; perturbing one entry of N_1 off-symmetric breaks it.
CHECK sp_coordinates_40: PASS — sp_params(N)[:40] == fq_leadsolve.mu_params(N_1, N_2, N_3); sp_mats(par40 + 35 zeros) reproduces fq_leadsolve.params_to_mats(par40) and has N_4 = N_5 = N_6 = 0 (BLOCKS offsets 0/15/25 with PAIRS1/PAIRS2/PAIRS1 as in fq_mfit).

(2a) CHECK class_cov: PASS — expanding (b_1, b_3, b_5) gives exactly N_k = b_k diag(zeta^{-ki}) for k = 1, 3, 5 and N_2 = N_4 = N_6 = 0; covariance (N_k)_{i+1,j+1} = zeta^{-k}(N_k)_{ij} holds for all k, i, j (random b); the b_1, b_3 columns restricted to the first 40 coordinates equal the (a1, a3) columns of fq_leadsolve.class_covariant_diagonal, the b_5 column is supported only on the k = 5 block (so b_5 = 0 reproduces the genus-2 class exactly).
(2b) class_circ — derivation: with (N_k)_{ij} = zeta^{-ki} c_k(j-i) and N_k^T = (-1)^{k+1} N_k: (N_k)_{ji} = zeta^{-kj} c_k(i-j) must equal (-1)^{k+1} zeta^{-ki} c_k(j-i); with d = j-i this is c_k(-d) = (-1)^{k+1} zeta^{k(j-i)} c_k(d) = (-1)^{k+1} zeta^{kd} c_k(d), i.e. c_k(5-d) = (-1)^{k+1} zeta^{kd} c_k(d). d = 0 gives c_k(0) = (-1)^{k+1} c_k(0), so c_k(0) = 0 for even k; d = 1, 2 are free and fix d = 4, 3: c_k(4) = (-1)^{k+1} zeta^k c_k(1), c_k(3) = (-1)^{k+1} zeta^{2k} c_k(2). Count: odd k: 3 parameters x 3 = 9, even k: 2 x 3 = 6, total 15. The code's `red` table is exactly {3: (2, sgn zeta^{2k}), 4: (1, sgn zeta^k)} with sgn = (-1)^{k+1}.
CHECK class_circ_construction: PASS — my own matrices built from the derived constraints equal sp_mats(expand(class_circ cols, t)) for random t (all 7 blocks), lie in sp and are Z/5-covariant.
CHECK class_circ_spans_covariant_subspace: PASS — the covariance equations (150 linear forms on the 75 coordinates) have nullspace dimension 15; rank(class_circ columns) = 15; rank(columns + nullspace basis) = 15; every column satisfies all covariance equations. So class_circ is EXACTLY the Z/5-covariant subspace of sp mod zhat^7.
(2c) CHECK class_circ_first40: PASS — the first 8 columns restricted to coordinates 0..39 equal fq_leadsolve.class_circulant with the same names and order (c1_0, c1_1, c1_2, c2_1, c2_2, c3_0, c3_1, c3_2); columns 1..8 vanish on coordinates 40..74 and columns 9..15 vanish on 0..39.
CHECK class_diag_first40 (extra): PASS — equals fq_leadsolve.modes_diagonal (X_a -> X1_a, Y_a -> X3_a).

(3) CHECK MU_exact_large_K: PASS — for K = 19 and 25, both placements, 3 random eps: MU.at(eps).M == M_0 exp(eps N_1 + eps^2 N_2 + eps^3 N_3) (right) / exp(..) M_0 (left) mod zhat^7, MU.at(eps).Minv == exp(-X) M_0^{-1} (right) / M_0^{-1} exp(-X) (left), M Minv = 1; own 7-term matrix exponential and own series product. Maximal u-degree of any entry 18 (= 3 KMAX), so K = 19 is exact.
CHECK MU_Taylor_coefficients: PASS — the K = 19 u-polynomial entries of M and Minv (7 x 25 each) equal the Taylor coefficients obtained by my own 19-node Vandermonde interpolation of the exact exponential at eps = 1..19; for K = 1, 2, 4, 6 the entries are exactly the truncations mod u^K of those series (K coefficients per entry), MU.check() True, and at(random eps) differs from the exact exponential (as it must for K <= 18).
CHECK MU_left: PASS — 'left' entries (K = 19 exact, K = 4 truncated) equal the Taylor coefficients of exp(..) M_0; left != right generically.
CHECK conj: PASS — conj(M0, N') = M_0^{-1} N' M_0 (own product), in sp; exp(eps N') M_0 == M_0 exp(eps conj(N')) at 3 random eps (own exponential); MU(left, [N'], K=7) == MU(right, [conj N'], K=7) entrywise (M and Minv); with three N's at K = 19 likewise (Ad is a homomorphism).
CHECK MU_identity_edge_case: PASS — MU(identity, [], 5) is the identity series, is_identity = False as documented.
Note (ref6_at_check.py): MU.at(eps, check=True) raises "not symplectic at zhat^2" for K = 6 and passes for K = 19: at(eps) at small K is the truncated polynomial, symplectic only mod u^K. The code uses check=False in UVertex, which is the correct usage (only [eps^e], e < K, is read after interpolation and the truncation does not affect those coefficients).

(4) Setup Rows(R, Nz=6), Conifold(R, Nu=10), SRows(rows, C, prec_abs=34), Symbol(S): 1.2 s; val_ok True.
CHECK colour_matrices: PASS — own C_n[j][i] = Sum_ab Rh[b][j][0] eta^{ba} Rh[a][i][n] equals Symbol.colour_matrix() (7 matrices), C_0 = 1; C(zhat)^T C(-zhat) = 1 mod zhat^7 (all 7 defect matrices zero; Symbol.symplectic_check(6): 0 failures); C_n is Z/5-circulant with phase zeta^{-n} and colour-mixing (120 non-zero off-diagonal entries for n = 1..6).
CHECK M0_from_symbol: PASS — M0.M[k] == C_k, M0.Minv[k] == (-1)^k C_k^T, Sum_a M_a Minv_{k-a} = delta_{k0}, own exp(mu) == C, mu in sp, checks dict {'exp_log': True, 'mu_in_sp': True, 'symbol_sympl': True}.
CHECK KEY_frozen_rows: PASS — own arithmetic: Q'_{a,n}|_{u=0} = Sum_{k<=n} Sum_j Rh[a][j][n-k] (Minv_k)_{ji} equals Rh[a][i][0] for n = 0 and 0 for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, all (a, i): R^ M_0^{-1} = R^(0) + O(zhat^7), maximal n = 6 (the full range available at Nz = 6; it is an identity Q_a^{(i)}(zhat) = Sum_j Rh^{(j)}_{a,0} C_{ji}(zhat), so it would hold for every n for which C_n exists). Via fq3_m.rows_prime6 on HatRowsU(S, 6) (.coef(0)) and on FrozenRows(sym): identical result. The [u^1] primed entries with n >= 1 are non-zero in 125 of 150 cases, so R' = 1 + O(u) and not more.
CHECK rows_prime6: PASS — identity short-circuit returns S.Q; with a MConst the result equals my own Ser convolution entry by entry (values and precision). HatRowsU(S, 6): val_ok True, min_prec 6 (= K by the truncation; the untruncated rows have >= 6 u-coefficients since the production check "min_prec >= K" passed), symbol_check True.
CHECK tc_coefficients: PASS — t_c = u + 7/10 u^2 + 41/75 u^3 + 9/20 u^4 at both primes; g3_state_89.json 'tc' residues match these rationals.

(5) Hatted theory at genus 3 — derivation: Qhat_{a,n} = Q_{a,n} s^{4n+1-c_a}, xhat = x/s, Deltahat_i^{1/2} = zeta^{4i} xhat; for any M(zhat) constant in u read in the z-variable as M(z) = Sum_k M_k s^{-4k} z^k, a vertex tensor of psi-deficit D_v is a polynomial of M-weight D_v in the M_k, hence carries s^{-4 D_v} in the genuine theory, so hatted vertex = s^{4 D_v - (2g_v-2+n_v)} x genuine vertex; an edge E'(a, a') is bilinear in Q'_{.,M} Q'_{.,N} with M + N = a + a' + 1 on eta-pairs (c_a + c_b = 2), so Ehat' = s^{4(a+a'+1)} E'; a leaf T'_d = (-1)^d Q'_{0,d-1} gives That'_d = s^{4d-3} T'_d. For a genus-g graph with E edges, m leaves: Sum_v (2g_v-2+n_v) = 2g-2+m and the dimension constraint Sum_h a_h + Sum_l d_l + Sum_v D_v = Sum_v (3g_v-3+n_v) = 3g-3-E+m. Total exponent: 4 Sum D_v - (2g-2+m) + 4 Sum a_h + 4E + 4 Sum d_l - 3m = 4(3g-3-E+m) - (2g-2+m) + 4E - 3m = 10(g-1), for EVERY decoration. Since the hatted rows and xhat are pure u-series (asserted at construction in HatRowsU.s_to_u) the hatted sum G_Gamma is a u-series and the genuine term is T_Gamma = s^{-10(g-1)} G_Gamma = u^{-2(g-1)} G_Gamma(u): u^{-4} at genus 3, regular at the conifold point iff [u^0..u^3] G_Gamma = 0 (t_c = u(1 + ...) is a regular reparametrisation). t_c conversion: with u = t w(t), w = 1 - c_1 t + (2c_1^2 - c_2) t^2 + (-5c_1^3 + 5c_1c_2 - c_3) t^3 + ..., u^{-4} G = t^{-4}[a_0 w^{-4} + a_1 t w^{-3} + a_2 t^2 w^{-2} + a_3 t^3 w^{-1}] gives
  t_c^{-4}: a_0;  t_c^{-3}: a_1 + 4 c_1 a_0;  t_c^{-2}: a_2 + 3 c_1 a_1 + (2 c_1^2 + 4 c_2) a_0;  t_c^{-1}: a_3 + 2 c_1 a_2 + 3 c_2 a_1 + 4 c_3 a_0
(the t_c^{-1} coefficient is the residue, Res_u u^{-4} G (dt_c/du), which confirms the last line independently; the genus-2 specialisation reproduces a_1 + 2c_1 a_0 and a_2 + c_1 a_1 + (2c_2 - c_1^2) a_0 of OU_EXTENSION s.1).
CHECK tc_expansion3_formulas: PASS — exact rationals (QRing), 3 random (a, c) with c_1 = 7/10: tc_expansion3 t_c^{-4..-1} == hand formulas == independent brute force (fixed-point reversion); with 6 u-coefficients it returns 6 t_c-coefficients, all equal to brute force; F_p with the actual conifold t_c at 2^61-1 and 2^89-1: equal to the hand formulas, and the g = 2 reduction equals fq_hat.tc_expansion and the genus-2 hand formula. Side result: the vertex graph has polar part (1/25200) t_c^{-4} + 0 + 0 + 0 iff its u-coefficients are a_0 = 1/25200, a_1 = -1/9000, a_2 = 407/3780000, a_3 = -151/3780000 (both primes).
CHECK hatted_count_direct_s_series (non-trivial M): PASS — with a RANDOM constant symplectic M of order 6 (not the identity), the genuine graph term computed directly in the s-variable (SRows rows, Ser-valued M^{-1}_k s^{-4k}, vertex tensors scaled by s^{-4D}) has valuation exactly -20 and equals s^{-20} G_Gamma(s^5) from HatRowsU/GraphSummer6 through s^{-10} (the row precision prec_abs = 34 allows no more), is a pure u-series, and differs from the M = 1 term; graphs 1 (vertex, E = 0), 2 and 5 (E = 1), 3 (E = 2, gv = (1,)). This is the first direct check of the count at genus 3 for M != 1 (the production step1_sseries only tests M = 1).

MAJOR issues: none found. Every claim of fq3_m.py in my scope (sp parametrisation, classes, M_0 = R~ mod zhat^7 with Minv_k = (-1)^k C_k^T, MU bivariate exponential and inverse, placements, conj, rows_prime6) and the genus-3 hatted-theory claims of fq3_msum.py (u^{-2(g-1)} count, regularity criterion, tc_expansion3) were reproduced with independent code.

MINOR issues:
- fq3_m.MU.at docstring "MConst at u = eps" is literally true only for K >= 19 (exact u-degree 18); for the production K = 6 at(eps) is the mod-u^K truncated polynomial evaluated at eps, which is NOT symplectic (at(eps, check=True) raises "not symplectic at zhat^2"). The code relies on this only through UVertex, where it is correct (truncating M^{-1} mod u^K leaves the eps^e coefficients, e < K, of every vertex tensor unchanged), but a reader could misuse at(eps) as an exact M(eps). Suggest a docstring note.
- fq3_m.MU drops N_j with j >= K silently (`if j >= K: break`); harmless (they cannot enter mod u^K) but undocumented.
- (4) "maximal n" is bounded by Nz = 6 only; the identity Q_a^{(i)} = Sum_j Rh^{(j)}_{a,0} C_{ji} makes R^ M_0^{-1} constant to every available order, so this check cannot fail for any Nz and is a consistency check of colour_matrix/Minv, not new information.
- HatRowsU.min_prec is computed after truncation to K, so the production check "min_prec >= K" is equivalent to "untruncated precision >= K" — correct but reads oddly.

Not independently established here (out of scope or not re-run):
- Correctness of the vertex tensors MVertex6 (other referee) and of the genus-3 graph list fq3_graphs (other referee); my s-series control uses MVertex6 on both sides, so it tests the hatting/valuation bookkeeping of fq3_msum/fq3_m, not the vertex CohFT itself.
- The hatted count for u-DEPENDENT M (MU through rows_prime6 Ser path + UVertex): verified only algebraically (the identity holds for all constant M, so substituting u-series M_k(u) preserves it) and by the module's own consistency checks; a direct s-series evaluation with M(zhat; u) at genus 3 was not run (the analogous direct check was done by the genus-2 referee).
- UVertex degree bound 3D <= 18: verified for the M^{-1} entries (max u-degree 18 observed), the implication for weight-D tensors is by the polynomial argument, not by a run.
- Rows/Conifold/SRows/Symbol themselves (trusted genus-2 modules) were used as given.

CHECK indep_enumeration_counts: PASS — independent enumerator (own canonical form: partition refinement + within-cell permutations; direct enumeration of edge multisets/genus vectors/leg maps with V <= 2g-2+n) vs fq3_graphs.legged_graphs, counts per E identical for all 9 cases: (2,0,3) [1,2,2,2]=7; (3,0,6) [1,2,5,9,12,8,5]=42; (2,1,4) [1,2,5,5,3]=16; (2,2,5) [1,4,13,24,23,10]=75; (3,1,5) [1,3,10,26,44,51]=135; (1,4,4) [1,12,43,68,39]=163; (1,3,3) [1,5,10,7]=23; (0,6,3) [1,25,105,105]=236; (0,5,2) [1,10,15]=26. Literature values I am sure of and that agree: Mbar_2 has 7 strata; Mbar_{0,6}: 25 boundary divisors (2^5-1-6), 105 = 7!! trivalent trees with 6 labelled leaves; Mbar_{0,5}: 10 divisors, 15 points. Mbar_3 = 42 confirmed by my enumeration only (E-distribution 1,2,5,9,12,8,5).

- fq3_graphs.canon brute-forces all V! permutations per degeneration: legged_graphs(3,1,5)/(1,4,4) take minutes (my compare run: 5 min total, of which the independent enumerator took < 1 s). Correctness unaffected.
